# Spiritual Translation : On the Formation of Genuine Wis doms in the Natural Mind

** ¶9. ** Genuine wisdoms do not arise in every condition of the natural mind, nor are they formed throughout the whole of natural knowledge. Rather , only in certain particular states within the natural mind are wis doms brought forth. For divine love blaz es from above and descends into the natural mind , and where it meets the field of natural knowledge it produces the first external appearances of truth — as when celest ial infl ux encounters out ward memory - knowledge and st irs it into a preliminary doctrinal form. Divine truth flows down from the celestial realm into these ou termost forms; and pur ified natural truths receive it , drawing it toward themselves within the natural mind.

**¶10.** This individual influx of divine truth descends into the purified natural truths and is absorbed by them, and they are con joined. The infl ux does not sink into the deep est obsc ur ities of merely natural knowledge; instead it remains at the level of conscious awareness, accessible within the mind . Around this whol esome infl ux, an external doctrinal form takes shape — first as a preliminary appearance , then as a fir mer containing vessel — and within it , a genuine wisdom begins to crystall ize. Yet when divine truth cannot be received whole, it breaks apart and is distributed into many lesser portions , each requiring its own time of purification before it can become a truth made good and recept ive. When at last celest ial truth and purified natural truth meet within the natural mind, and they are accommod ated within the external doctrinal form — which at first was only the ou termost appearance — they are con joined with one another and are shaped into a great and precious wisdom of full worth .

**¶11.** When, however, an infl ux of divine truth desc ends and that infl ux is frag mented into many lesser portions and various scattered particles of understanding , these are formed into and enclosed within numerous smaller wisdoms, each held in its own external doctrinal vessel . One containing form may shelter two wis doms, another may shelter three, others may shelter five; some hold more than these, some fewer.

**¶12.** Now , when a whole and und ivided influx of divine truth is received, and the containing doc trinal form receives it intact , it becomes a great and precious wisdom, its perf ection complete . Yet even if the truth has been divided into lesser portions, if these portions have time to adhere to one another before any understanding is lost, and they are conjoined with each other, and the containing form en closes them before they scatter further — then they too may be shaped into a great wisdom, and the celest ial infl ux together with the purified natural tru ths within them forms a great and valued good .

**¶13.** Behold, I have shown how genuine wisdoms are formed within the natural mind. I have told you that just as wisdom comes into existence by means of divine truth that has time to be received into preliminary appearances , the external doctrinal form comes into existence by means of those appearances , and those very appearances arise from the transformation and the working of the natural mind itself under infl ux.

**¶14.** Then , when those who possess spiritual perception — who search the depths of the natural mind — recognize the time , they desc end into those particular states and bring wis doms up from the obsc ur ities of natural knowledge into the light . Each one who searches finds according to the providence that is ordained for him . These seek ers deliver what they find to those who transm it and communicate wisdom , and those transmitters deliver it in turn to the ruling loves of the will and to the governing principles of the understanding — to whatever is sovereign in the mind .

**¶17.** For all the interior aff ections that rise up through the natural and corpor eal state of human life and are lib erated from it shall be restored to the great heav enly states of wisdom and love . A state of peace comes about for them , a dwelling - place within the celest ial real ms of the Divine Great ness.

Now, in] that sea, in which the [pearls] shall be formed[,] this [is the way of their formation:] what the sea shall [cast forth from] its fire above and comes [down upon the waters,] and it makes foam like the drop of water that flows [from above] down in rainwater[. This] is the water [that comes d]own first [into the] foam and comes down [to] the sweet waters[, and they receive] the waters.

"When, however, a drop of rainwater falls, and that drop breaks into many droplets and various , they shall be formed into and be confined in [n]umerous pearls, in the shell and the pearl-shell. One might form two pearls, another may form three, others may form five; some mould more than these, some fewer.

"Now, when you might [find a] whole drop, and the shell receives it, it shall become a great and valued [pe]arl as its worth is perfected. [However], if these two droplets will have time (to adhere) to one another before any (water particle) escapes, and they mix with e[ach o]ther, and the shell [encloses them] before they break into [many parts] within [it, and they are shaped] in a great kind[. For] the drop of rain, which [combines with] another one, that [comes forth from] the [w]aters form them in [a pearl, and] in a great, valued commodity.

"Behold, [I, I have] taught you how sea-pearls shall be formed. I have told you that as a pearl shall come into existence by means of rainwater that has [ti]me to become foam, the pearl-shell shall come into existence by means of the foam, and the foam itself comes into being by means of the transformation and the [working] of the sea.

"Then immediately at the time when [the pearls are formed,] the pearl divers know it, they shall [come,] and they [go d]own to those places and they bring pearls up from the depths of the sea, and each pearl diver finds according to the fortune that is [ordai]ned for him. The pearl divers shall [gi]ve them to the traders, and the traders give them to the kings and the nobles.

"Fo[r a]ll the souls that ascend in the flesh of mankind and are freed shall be brought back to the great aeons of light. A place of rest comes about for them, at that place in the aeons of greatness.

"This drop of water shall [come] down to the sweet waters and [they receive it,] and they absorbed them and were combined with the [sweet waters]. They did not [d]escend to the depths of the sea, but they [remained above, and] it floated on the surface of the waters [and was drawn close] to it. The foam and the pearl-shell shall be formed [around] this wholesome drop [and shall enclose] it, and it becomes a pe[arl. But the force] that makes a drop of rainwater [fall to the] waters [with] it not being whole. It breaks and separates out into many droplets, and it has time to become a drop of sweet water [once more,] and comes up in the sea of [the] rain and sweet water; and it is accomodated in the shell, which at first is foam. They shall be joined with each other at [this] time, and are shaped and become a great pea[r]l, a great and valued kind.
